question_text:
Estimate the plasma frequency \(\left(v_{p}\right)\) of lithium metal using the atomic density of lithium metal.
The unit of the answer is Hz.
response:
## Reasoning

The plasma frequency (angular) is

$$\omega_p = \sqrt{\frac{n e^2}{m_e \varepsilon_0}}$$

and the ordinary frequency is $\nu_p = \omega_p/(2\pi)$.

For lithium (a monovalent metal), the conduction electron density equals the atomic density:

$$n = \frac{\rho N_A}{M}$$

Using lithium's density $\rho = 0.534\ \text{g/cm}^3 = 534\ \text{kg/m}^3$, molar mass $M = 6.941\ \text{g/mol}$, and $N_A = 6.022\times10^{23}\ \text{mol}^{-1}$:

$$n = \frac{534 \times 6.022\times10^{23}}{6.941\times10^{-3}} \approx 4.63\times10^{28}\ \text{m}^{-3}$$

Then

$$\omega_p = \sqrt{\frac{(4.63\times10^{28})(1.602\times10^{-19})^2}{(9.109\times10^{-31})(8.854\times10^{-12})}} \approx 1.21\times10^{16}\ \text{rad/s}$$

$$\nu_p = \frac{\omega_p}{2\pi} \approx 1.93\times10^{15}\ \text{Hz}$$

$$\boxed{1.93\times10^{15}}$$
